q-214561.name: Question 1
q-214561.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $a.$ To do this, we first add $2$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =-14ab-2 \\ 5+2 & =-14ab-2+2 \\ 7 & =-14ab\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $-14b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7 & =-14ab \\ \frac{7}{-14b} & =\frac{-14ab}{-14b} \\ \frac{7}{-14b} & =\frac{\cancel{-14b}a}{\cancel{-14b}} \\ -\frac{7}{14b} & =a\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{7}{7\cdot 2b} & =a \\ -\frac{\cancel{7}}{\cancel{7}\cdot 2b} & =a \\ -\frac{1}{2b} & =a \\ a & =-\frac{1}{2b}\end{aligned}
$$

q-133665.name: Question 3
q-133665.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $10$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{3}{10}hk \\ 10\cdot 2 & =10\cdot \frac{3}{10}hk \\ 20 & =3hk\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to isolate $k.$ To do this, we divide both sides of the equation by $3h:$

$$
\begin{aligned}20 & =3hk \\ \frac{20}{3h} & =\frac{3hk}{3h} \\ \frac{20}{3h} & =\frac{\cancel{3h}k}{\cancel{3h}} \\ \frac{20}{3h} & =k \\ k & =\frac{20}{3h}\end{aligned}
$$

q-133663.name: Question 4
q-133663.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $3$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} & =5vs \\ 3\cdot \frac{4}{3} & =3\cdot 5vs \\ 4 & =15vs\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to isolate $s.$ To do this, we divide both sides of the equation by $15v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =15vs \\ \frac{4}{15v} & =\frac{15vs}{15v} \\ \frac{4}{15v} & =\frac{\cancel{15v}s}{\cancel{15v}} \\ \frac{4}{15v} & =s \\ s & =\frac{4}{15v}\end{aligned}
$$

q-214615.name: Question 5
q-214615.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $y.$ To do this, we first cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3xy}{10} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{-3xy}{10} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\cdot (-3xy) & =10\cdot 1 \\ -6xy & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $-6x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6xy & =10 \\ \frac{-6xy}{-6x} & =\frac{10}{-6x} \\ \frac{\cancel{-6x}\,y}{\cancel{-6x}} & =\frac{10}{-6x} \\ y & =-\frac{10}{6x}\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{2\cdot 5}{2\cdot 3x} \\ y & =-\frac{\cancel{2}\cdot 5}{\cancel{2}\cdot 3x} \\ y & =-\frac{5}{3x}\end{aligned}
$$

q-75488.name: Question 6
q-75488.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $x.$ To do this, we first cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12nx}{2} & =\frac{4}{7} \\ 7\cdot 12nx & =2\cdot 4 \\ 84nx & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $84n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}84nx & =8 \\ \frac{84nx}{84n} & =\frac{8}{84n} \\ \frac{\cancel{84n}x}{\cancel{84n}} & =\frac{8}{84n} \\ x & =\frac{8}{84n}\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{4\cdot 2}{4\cdot 21n} \\ x & =\frac{\cancel{4}\cdot 2}{\cancel{4}\cdot 21n} \\ x & =\frac{2}{21n}\end{aligned}
$$

121n

142n
e
221n
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to isolate x. To do this, we first cross-multiply: 12nx2=477⋅12nx=2⋅484nx=8

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by 84n: 84nx=884nx84n=884n84nx84n=884nx=884n

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows: x=4⋅24⋅21nx=4⋅24⋅21nx=221n
